title: operator-change-decision-log-and-mini-evidence-playbook
body:
Goal: Define a small-footprint decision log format and accompanying operator playbook for customer-managed networking changes that balances forensic needs with low-bandwidth environments.

Context and motivation:
- Customers running Redwood Private often have constrained observability pipelines (low egress, intermittent connectivity). They request a compact, verifiable evidence artifact for network/operator changes so audits and rollbacks are feasible without shipping full syslogs.
- Existing proposals in the folder focus on full audit envelopes; this doc proposes a minimal decision log that can be produced on-device (edge/operator sidecar) and later expanded or reconciled with richer telemetry.

Non-goals:
- Not replacing full SIEM-forwarding or long-term archival policies.
- Not defining cryptographic escrow services (we reference KMS/HSM integration separately).

High-level approach:
1) Define a compact JSONL decision-log record with a strict, small schema (see "sample record" below). Records are signed (optional HMAC) and append-only.
2) Provide an operator runbook for the common change categories (config update, firewall rule, route peering, key rotation) that maps to required evidence fields and approval-gate checkpoints.
3) Establish two-mode workflows: online (can push full evidence immediately) and offline (compact record only, sync later).

User stories:
- As a customer operator, I want a one-line change record that proves "who approved what" so I can satisfy compliance reviewers even if full logs are offline.
- As Redwood SRE, I want the compact record to be machine-parseable so automated triage and rollback helpers can act on it.
- As an auditor, I want to be able to request the expanded evidence bundle if the compact log indicates a high-risk change.

Mini-decision-log schema (design goals: <1KB typical, human-readable, strict keys):
- id: short UUID (v4)
- ts: ISO8601 UTC timestamp of the change decision
- actor: operator id (email or principal)
- action: short enum (CONFIG_PATCH | FIREWALL_RULE | PEER_ADD | KEY_ROTATE | ROLLBACK_TRIGGER)
- target: short string identifying component (e.g., cust-edge-1/nat1)
- rationale: one-line summary (max 140 chars)
- approval: small object substitute encoded as a string of the form "role:approver|method" (examples below)
- evidence_refs: comma-separated short tokens pointing to local artifacts (e.g., cfg-v2, ticket-147)
- signature: optional HMAC-SHA256 hex of the canonical line using local operator secret
- flags: comma-separated quick tags (e.g., emergency, canary, scheduled)

Note: agents.md requires metadata entries be flat lists/strings; schema above is for the log payloads produced at runtime, not nested in Drive JSON.

Sample record (compact, as a single canonical line):
{"id":"d4f2a9c1","ts":"2025-11-04T18:12:03Z","actor":"emma@acme-corp","action":"FIREWALL_RULE","target":"cust-edge-32/nat","rationale":"open port 443 for svc-x rollout","approval":"eng-operator:liam.chen|ui-confirm","evidence_refs":"ticket-2123,preflight-scan-7","signature":"3f5b...a8c9","flags":"canary"}

Operator playbook (quick steps for each change class):
- CONFIG_PATCH:
  1) Create a decision record pre-change with id, ts, actor, action=CONFIG_PATCH, target, rationale="patch:<short>".
  2) Attach evidence_refs: local diff summary token (diff-<n>), PR or ticket id.
  3) If change passes approval gate (manual or automated), signature HMAC is computed and appended.
  4) Execute patch; append a follow-up record with action=CONFIG_PATCH_COMPLETE and delta notes in evidence_refs.
- FIREWALL_RULE:
  1) Provide minimal risk assessment tag (low/medium/high) in flags.
  2) Require secondary approver for high. Represent approval as "sec-approver:email|2fa" in approval field.
- PEER_ADD / PEER_REMOVE:
  1) Require proof-of-ownership: evidence_refs must include the peer ASN or certificate fingerprint token.
  2) If offline, embed base64 short cert fingerprint in evidence_refs token (prefixed fp:).
- KEY_ROTATE:
  1) Record key id and rotation window in rationale.
  2) Evidence_refs must include rotation-ticket and KMS-change-id; trigger an immediate sync to control plane if available.

Approval gate definitions (minimal):
- auto-approve: Triggered when change is low-risk and matches a pre-approved template (exact match of target+action+rationale token). "approval" set to "auto:template-<id>".
- manual-approve: Requires operator confirmation in console or signed HMAC. "approval" example "op:emma@acme|ui".
- dual-approval: For high-risk, require two distinct actors; encode as "op:email1+email2|2fa".

Offline sync model:
- Decision records are stored locally in append-only file compressed with chunked rotation.
- A compact sync tool uploads batches when connectivity returns. Each upload batch includes batch_id, min_ts, max_ts and a manifest sha256.
- Control plane validates signatures/approvals against known operator public keys (or HMAC secrets known to the customer-agent during enterprise setup).

Forensics and escalation flow:
1) If a decision record is marked high-risk or flagged by automated monitors, Redwood can make a request for expanded evidence bundle. The bundle should include: short config diff (text), prechange test result, short pcap (if applicable) — but always with a maximum size cap and with customer consent options.
2) If bundle is not retrievable (offline), the compact record plus operator attestations are used for triage; action windows may be restricted (e.g., require rollback capability before approving further changes).

Integration points with product: console, operator sidecar, approval API
- Console: render compact decision list, enable manual approve/deny, display flag badges and link to ticket/evidence_refs.
- Sidecar: produce signed compact records, expose local CLI for forced sync, provide tooling to export a zip of expanded artifacts when asked.
- Approval API: endpoints to POST compact records, request expanded bundle, and to fetch batch manifests.

Observability and SLOs:
- Metric: compact-record-success-rate (target >99%) for online mode.
- Metric: batch-sync-latency p50/p95 for offline uploads.
- Alert: missing follow-up records for changes older than 24h (indicates incomplete evidence).

Security considerations:
- HMAC secrets must be provisioned via customer KMS; do not store plain secrets in sidecar.
- Compact records leak minimal context by design; avoid embedding sensitive tokens.
- Signed records should include a verification path in control-plane but verification must always respect customer-managed key material policies.

Acceptance criteria / minimal MVP:
- Sidecar can create compact decision records for the four change classes and persist them locally.
- Console can ingest and render these records, searchable by id and actor.
- Approval API can accept signed records and verify HMAC with a preconfigured secret.
- Offline batch sync implemented with manifest verification and idempotent ingest.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Do we require asymmetric signatures (certs) for all customers or HMAC is sufficient? (HMAC is lower friction but requires shared secret management.)
- How large should the evidence_refs token pool be (limit to 6 tokens?) to keep record compact but searchable?
- Customer UX for "request expanded bundle": automated vs manual gating and consent flows.

Next steps / near-term plan:
- Prototype sidecar that emits the sample record above and a simple batch sync tool (2 week spike).
- Run a pilot with two midmarket customers that have low-egress constraints to validate bundle requests and the forensics flow (4 week pilot).
- Decision on crypto: escalate to security for recommendation (1 week).

Appendix: example quick checklist for operator before pushing change
- Did you create a compact decision record? (Y/N)
- Is the approval field populated? (Y/N)
- If high-risk, did you record a secondary approver? (Y/N)
- Will this change require expanded evidence later? (flag it)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive and compact — trying to cover a gap observed in early customer pilots where operators had only ephemeral proof.
- Feedback requested on the approval encoding and whether a tiny structured object (e.g., approval_method, approvers list) would materially improve parsing at the cost of size.

Local references: see linked Confluence page for broader attestation patterns and the GH issue for the sync tool prototype.
